detail.instructions: Update commit in src/infrastructure/sqlite_repository.rs. Explicitly roll back after UPDATE, INSERT, or stored-ID validation failure; map the original Database or InvalidStoredData error only when rollback succeeds, otherwise return CommitOutcomeUnknown. A zero-row conditional update returns UnavailableAtCommit only after successful rollback. Map an error from transaction.commit() to CommitOutcomeUnknown. Do not retry. Use supplied triggers to verify statement rollback and deferred-constraint commit failure.

files.content: // Response mapping is implemented in a later lesson.

hints.body: Do not classify transaction-time errors as Database just because the failing statement ran before COMMIT. First wait for rollback; rollback failure keeps outcome unknown.

A small rollback helper can consume the transaction and preserve a supplied result only when rollback succeeds. Use it for statement errors, invalid returned IDs, and the zero-row unavailable outcome.
Map update/insert errors to Database and invalid returned IDs to InvalidStoredData through confirmed rollback. Leave COMMIT errors as CommitOutcomeUnknown and never retry.

detail.completionExplanation: The insert failure is a known failure only after rollback succeeds. A COMMIT error remains CommitOutcomeUnknown, so the service must not tell the customer the order definitely failed or silently submit it again. The final lesson follows the successful path to its HTTP response—and what happens if that response is lost.
